newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE may fall to 4,640 after initial rise.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE may fall to 4,640 after initial rise.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index may creep up towards 4,700 on Wednesday following two days of sharp losses, but it will be difficult for the market to regain the upward thrust seen last week, technical analysts said.
Investors have been gripped by fear of what may be announced in the UK Budget in July that they may take further defensive action by taking profits on any stock market rallies.
Such action could see the index then fall away to around 4,640. And with June index options and futures expiring on Friday, investors should brace themselves for a bumpy ride, analysts say.
By 0720 GMT, the index was indicated up 3.0 at 4,685.2.
The FTSE has spun down 100 points over the past two days and seems to have more risk of probing lower support levels than of challenging resistance areas above 4,700, analysts said.
Financial and pharmaceuticals -- which had been the heavy weight sectors powering the market higher -- may now be more subdued and become a drag on the index, they added.

The market's distressed state was signalled on Tuesday when it went below its 10 day moving average and unless a swift recovery takes place, the FTSE will have to endure further downward pressure, analysts said.
Breadth in the broader market -- as measured by the number of stocks advancing to those declining -- also indicates further weakness to come.

Breadth readings for over 2,000 stocks yesterday slipped to one-to-two compared with a daily average of four-to-three last week and this confirms a weak background for the stock market, analysts said.
